_readme: THE APP'S OWN TAX FIGURES — the floor every country falls back to (item 4.81).
🔴 THESE ARE NEW ZEALAND'S, AND THAT IS THE DEFECT THE ITEM WAS FILED AGAINST. They are
not a considered default and must never be presented as one: 28% company tax, 15% GST, a
two-monthly filing cycle and the invoice basis are what the Three-Way Forecast has applied
to every client in every country since it was built. An Australian company is at 30% and
10% and files quarterly. Everything here is tagged `app default` on screen, in exactly
those words, so nobody reads it as sourced.
WHY THEY ARE STILL THE FALLBACK. Changing what an unconfigured firm gets would move every
existing forecast the moment this shipped, with nobody having approved anything. A figure
moves when a manager approves a document that moves it, and at no other time. So the
fallback reproduces TODAY'S behaviour exactly, and the fix is that a manager can now put a
sourced figure over it and an advisor can see which they are looking at.
WHY THE NUMBERS LIVE HERE RATHER THAN ONLY IN THE SCREEN. They were already declared twice
— the intake's own defaults in components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue (percentages, and the
two cycle/basis words) and the engine's defaults in server/report/threeWayForecastModel.js
(decimals). A cascading store needs a third reading of the same four figures, and three
copies is two too many. tests/unit/taxRates.test.js pins this file against the ENGINE's
defaults, which are the ones that actually compute a forecast, so the three cannot drift.
🔴 RATES ARE DECIMALS, 0..1 — 30% is 0.3, never 30. That is the engine's own convention
(it multiplies profit by taxRate directly) and the backend's convention everywhere else.
The intake SCREEN works in percentages and converts; the store never does.
`filing.months` IS A NUMBER OF MONTHS and `filing.label` is the country's own name for it.
Mike approved the split on 2026-09-09: the engine reads the number, a manager and an
advisor read the name. It is what lets Australia's quarterly BAS and the United Kingdom's
quarterly VAT exist at all — the engine held three hardcoded cycles, all of them New
Zealand's, and a three-month cycle could not be expressed.
`basis.basis` IS CANONICAL (`invoice` or `cash`) and `basis.label` is the country's own
word for it. New Zealand says Invoice, Australia says Accruals, and they are the same
thing; storing the country's word alone would give the engine two spellings of one rule.
`source` is null on every figure, and that is the point. A figure with no source document
is an app default; a figure WITH one came from a document a manager approved. The screen
tells them apart by exactly this field.
